sources.title: Fire towers are fading into history

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The only tower-specific source is the tnlandforms list entry (name, county, elevation, coordinates). The list's note puts names for towers 1 to 72 on a USGS name database, so the name is probably a map name, but no source confirms that. Elevation unit is not labelled; 253 is read as feet to match the record's 77.1 m. The community of Cedar Springs in Early County is cited only for its existence; no source links the tower to it. Do not merge with the Cedar Springs Lookout in New Mexico (nhlr.org, Rio Arriba County), which is a different tower. Two searches returned only topo-map, mapping and wildfire-incident pages. No source found on build date, design, staffing, status or access. The Savannah article was read from a web.archive.org copy because savannahnow.com returned 403.
